issues.failure_explanation: Combining Lemma truncation chaos M with Lemma approximation holder gives the per-order bound n!·κ²n²τ^{2β+n}M^{-2β}, so the correct intermediate sum is ∑_{n=1}^P n!n²τ^n, not ∑_{n=1}^P n/(n-1)! τ^n. The latter equals e^τ(τ+τ²) and is uniformly bounded in P, whereas the correct sum grows factorially in P (it is essentially sharp, e.g. for kernels g_n(u)=κ∑_k u_k^β). Hence the stated bound with a P-independent constant is false in general; the valid bound is κ²τ^{2β}(∑_{n=1}^P n!n²τ^n)M^{-2β}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace e^τ(τ+τ²) by ∑_{n=1}^P n!n²τ^n (absorbed into the P-dependent constant C_P) in the statement of Lemma approximation CpM; the main theorems need no further change.
issues.overall_effect: The basis-truncation lemma's stated constant cannot be independent of P. Theorem thm:added-4's second bound is unaffected in substance because it already allows C_P to depend on P; only the proof's invocation of the lemma needs the corrected (P-dependent) constant.
issues.title: Wrong summation in the proof of the basis-truncation error bound; stated P-independent constant is false
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma is false as written (its constant must grow with P), so a substantive quantitative claim is withdrawn; however the repair is a local correction of one summation and constant, the M^{-2β} rate and all downstream theorems survive, hence moderate rather than serious.

issues.failure_explanation: Both main error estimates are stated under only Assumption 1 (Lipschitz f, ξ ∈ L²), but their proofs combine: (i) Lemma lem:malliavin-energy, which assumes f ∈ C_{b,(y,z)}^{1:1} and uses the chain rule with bounded derivatives to control Df_i; (ii) the truncation bound E|f_i − C^P(f_i)|² ≤ E‖Df_i‖²/(P+1), which needs f_i ∈ D^{1,2}; (iii) the Euler error theorem (Theorem main convergence rate), which requires its own Malliavin regularity and Hölder assumptions on (ξ, f). Under the stated hypotheses the term E‖Dξ‖² may be infinite (making the bound vacuous) and the energy estimate is unavailable, so the theorems are not established as stated.

failure_location.quote: Let $\pi \subset [0,T]$ be a partition such that $\max_{i} \Delta_i / \Delta_{i+1} \leq L$. Let $\theta = (P,M) \in \mathbb{N}^{2}$. Let Assumption \ref{assumption 1} be satisfied.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypotheses to both theorems (f ∈ C_{b,(y,z)}^{1:1}, ξ ∈ D_T^{1,2}, and the assumptions of Theorem main convergence rate), or supply a standard mollification/approximation argument extending the estimates from smooth generators to Lipschitz ones.
issues.overall_effect: The two main error estimates (exact and Monte Carlo coefficient computation) are not proved under their advertised hypotheses; they are valid only under stronger smoothness/Malliavin assumptions on f and ξ.
issues.title: Main error estimates stated under Assumption 1 only, but the proofs require smooth f and Malliavin-regular ξ
issues.why_classification: The advertised hypothesis set (Assumption 1) is strictly weaker than what the proofs use, so the scope of the main theorems must be narrowed or an approximation argument added; the results themselves are standard and survive under slightly stronger but still standard assumptions, so the loss is contained and the issue is moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\hat{d}_{a}^{i}}{a!} \coloneqq \overline{\mathbb{E}} \Big( \widehat{Y}_{t_{i}}^{\pi, \theta, 0} \times H_{a}^{(i, 0)} \; \Big| \; \mathcal{F}^{i+1 \leq} \Big) + \frac{\Delta_{i}}{N} \sum_{n=1}^{N}  f(t_{i}, \widehat{Y}_{t_{i}}^{\pi, \theta, n}, \scalar{\widehat{Z}}_{i}^{\pi, \theta, n}) \times H_{a}^{(i, n)}

The random variables $\hat{d}_{a}^{i}$ are $\mathcal{F}^{i \leq}$-measurable. Moreover, for each $n\ge 1$, $\hat{d}_{a}^{i}$ is independent of $\widehat{H}_{a}^{(i, n)}$ (they are built from different Brownian families).

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed equality is false. The Monte Carlo part of d̂_a^i uses samples built from Brownian families independent of F^{i+1≤}, so it estimates the unconditional expectation E[f̂_i^{π,θ}H_a^{(i,0)}], whereas the chaos coefficient of F̂_i^{π,θ} w.r.t. B with F^{i+1≤}-measurable coefficients is a!·E[f̂_i^{π,θ}H_a^{(i,0)} | F^{i+1≤}]. Moreover f̂_i^{π,θ,0} depends on F^{i+1≤} through Ŷ^{π,θ,0}_{t_i} and Z̄^{π,θ,0}_i (which involve the F^{i+1≤}-measurable coefficients d̂^{i+1}), so the conditional and unconditional expectations differ. The correct relation is E[d̂_a^i | F^{i+1≤}] = a!E[Ŷ H_a | F^{i+1≤}] + Δ_i a!E[f̂ H_a] (unconditional in the f-part), and the subsequent projection identity used to bound the bias term does not hold as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false equality by the correct decomposition E[d̂_a^i | F^{i+1≤}] = a!E[Ŷ_{t_i}^{π,θ,0}H_a^{(i,0)} | F^{i+1≤}] + Δ_i a!E[f̂_i^{π,θ}H_a^{(i,0)}] and bound the bias term directly (projection bound for the Ŷ-part plus Cauchy–Schwarz/Young for the discrepancy E[f̂H_a|F^{i+1≤}] − E[f̂H_a]); adjust ε in the recursion of Lemma error implementation MC to absorb the extra Δ_iE|f̂−f|² term.
issues.overall_effect: The first inequality of Lemma MC (the per-step Monte Carlo error bound) is unproven as written; Lemma error implementation MC and Theorem thm:added-5, which rely on it, inherit the gap. The 1/N rate is unaffected: the bias term can still be bounded by (1+2Δ_i)E|F̂−F|² + 5Δ_iE|f̂−f|², and the extra Δ_iE|f̂−f|² term is absorbed by the Lipschitz recursion, so the final error bounds survive with modified constants.
issues.title: False conditional-expectation identity in the Monte Carlo error analysis of the chaos coefficients
issues.why_classification: The false equality is a genuine logical gap in the central Monte Carlo error analysis, and its repair requires a replacement estimate for the bias term; however the repair is contained, needs no new proof architecture, and all advertised rates and final error bounds survive with changed constants, so the issue is moderate.
